first.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing makes memory_73 (promotional pricing) the intuitive pull, which is exactly why it deserves the first verification slot: it is the most load-bearing and also the most suspiciously expansive memory in the set. It carries four distinct claims (acquisition lift, revenue lift, faster time-to-first-value, generalization across both billing plans) consolidated from a single day-31 record. Consolidated summaries tend to accumulate scope they never earned, and discount-driven acquisition is the classic case where a headline revenue lift masks lower-quality, higher-churn accounts. Under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, matching a competitor on price is also the move most likely to trade durable margin for a quarter of vanity numbers, so I want the original record before I let it drive anything. Second verification goes to memory_31, because it is the memory I currently intend to act on. Its mechanism is explicitly 'cutting required fields at signup,' which is not value-neutral: fewer fields means less qualification data, which can push unqualified volume downstream and degrade the very metric I am optimizing. I want to know whether the original experiment measured downstream qualified pipeline or only first-week activation, and whether 'durable' was actually observed over time or asserted at consolidation. Intent, held loosely: simplify_onboarding. The two live symptoms are declining onboarding completion (-4%) and declining activation (-6%), and memory_31 and memory_86 converge independently on that funnel stage, so this addresses mechanism rather than symptom. The competitor pressure is real but discounting responds to it by conceding the frame. Caveats I am not resolving away: memory_86 and memory_31 may be two consolidations of overlapping work, so their agreement could be one finding double-counted rather than genuine replication. All of this evidence is 15-64 days old and predates the current competitive environment. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout, with explicit guardrails on downstream lead quality and qualified-pipeline conversion, not just activation rate. If verification shows memory_31 never tracked downstream quality, I will narrow to a guarded test; if memory_73's record turns out to be well-instrumented on retention and the field-cutting risk looks material, promotional_pricing returns as a candidate.
